summary: The UK government says North Korea's borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and some limited tourism has restarted. It says tourists can normally travel only as part of an organised tour and independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs. A US Federal Register notice says US passports are invalid for travel to North Korea unless specially validated.

notes: The UK government advises against bringing books or other written material in the Korean language, including anything with religious content, and says customs officers will confiscate literature or media deemed anti-government, subversive or pornographic. Canada's travel advice says the same applies to material printed in South Korea.

The UK government says foreign mobile phones must be registered at the border and cannot connect to any network using an international SIM card, and that GPS devices must be left with customs until you leave. Canada's travel advice says importing satellite telephones and shortwave radios is prohibited, and that such items are confiscated on entry and usually returned on departure.

The UK government advises asking permission from your tour guide before taking any photographs; Canada's travel advice says photos or videos taken outside tourist areas could result in the confiscation of your equipment or detention.

payments.text: The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted, that the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies with Chinese yuan accepted in some places, and that importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice adds that there are no ATMs, that change in foreign currency is often unavailable, and that some hotels accept credit cards if you give them advance notice.

safety.text: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to North Korea. It says the North Korean authorities have previously detained foreign nationals for allegedly violating local laws and denied them access to support from their governments, and that a guide will almost always accompany visitors and decide where they can go. Canada advises avoiding all travel, citing the risk of arbitrary detention.

tips.text: The UK government advises against all but essential travel to North Korea, and Canada advises avoiding all travel, citing the risk of arbitrary detention. A US Federal Register notice says US passports are invalid for travel there unless specially validated.

The UK government says to ask permission from your tour guide before taking any photographs. Canada's travel advice says you must be accompanied by an official guide at all times, that authorities may seize material deemed pornographic, political or intended for religious proselytizing, as well as material printed in South Korea, and that you could be arrested and detained for unsanctioned political or religious activity.
The UK government says North Korea's borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and some limited tourism has restarted.

The UK government says a foreign mobile phone must be registered at the border and there is no connectivity to international or domestic mobile networks using an international SIM card, and that the routine lack of access to internet and mobile networks makes it almost impossible to communicate outside North Korea.

The UK government says the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies, with Chinese yuan accepted in some places. Canada's travel advice says change in foreign currency is often unavailable.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for North Korea?
faq.answer: Yes, for every passport whose rule we found on an official page: the UK, Canada, Germany, France, Italy and Estonia each say their citizens need a visa, and China says its citizens with ordinary private passports must obtain a visa or a tourist card before travelling; no official source we could read states the rule for other passports. The UK government says tourists can normally travel only as part of an organised tour, that independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs, and that the borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 with some limited tourism restarted. US passports are invalid for travel there unless specially validated.

faq.question: Can US citizens visit North Korea?
faq.answer: Not on a US passport unless it is specially validated. A US Federal Register notice says that on 1 September 2017 all US passports were declared invalid for travel to, in or through North Korea unless specially validated, that the restriction has been extended annually since 2017, and that the latest notice extends it until 31 August 2027.

faq.question: Is North Korea open to tourists in 2026?
faq.answer: Only in a limited way, according to the UK government: it says North Korea's borders have been closed to general entry since 2020 and that some limited tourism has restarted.

faq.question: Can I travel independently in North Korea?
faq.answer: Normally not. Canada's travel advice says you must be accompanied by an official guide at all times, and the UK government says a guide will almost always accompany you and will decide where you can go. The UK Foreign Office says tourists can normally travel only as part of an organised tour and that independent travellers need a sponsor and permission from the Ministry for Foreign Affairs.

faq.question: What money do tourists use in North Korea?
faq.answer: Mostly cash. The UK government says credit cards and international mobile payments are not accepted, that the US dollar and the euro are the most widely accepted currencies with Chinese yuan accepted in some places, and that importing or exporting the won is illegal. Canada's travel advice says cash is the most accepted form of payment and there are no ATMs, and that some hotels accept credit cards if you give them advance notice.
